path/two: Noise is easy to make: one random number per pixel. An image is harder, because its pixels must work together to make a face.
path/path: A diffusion model, a way to make images, starts by joining the two with a path that takes an image apart, a little at a time, until only noise is left.
path/ink: The name is from physics. A drop of ink in water spreads out, or diffuses, until its shape is gone.
path/sohl: In 2015, Yasha Sohl-Dickstein and colleagues proposed doing that to data: destroy its structure slowly, in many small steps of noise.
path/x0: The clean image is x zero: x at step zero, before any noise. Each pixel is one number.
path/eps: The noise is epsilon: one draw per pixel from a standard normal, the bell curve centered on zero, with a variance of one.
blend/xt: Every picture on the path blends the two ends. The one at step t is written x t.
blend/ab: How much of each goes in is set by one number, alpha bar: alpha, with a bar on top. Near one, the image has a light dusting of noise. At a half, the two are equally strong. Near zero, only a faint trace of the image is left.
blend/mix: The blend scales the image by the square root of alpha bar, the noise by the square root of one minus alpha bar, and adds them.
blend/roots: At an alpha bar of zero point six four, the image is scaled by zero point eight, and the noise by the root of zero point three six: zero point six.
blend/pixel: Follow a pixel of one, with noise of minus a half. zero point eight times one, plus zero point six times minus a half, is zero point five.
variance/keep: Why the roots? Say the clean pixels have a variance of one, like the noise. The blend keeps it at one, so the pixels stay as spread out, and only what they are made of changes.
variance/pair: Variance is the average squared distance from the mean. Pixels of one and minus one each sit one away from zero: a variance of one.
variance/rule: Scale both by zero point eight, and each sits zero point eight away: the variance is zero point six four. Scaling by any number, c, scales the variance by c squared.
variance/parts: So the image part, scaled by the root of alpha bar, has a variance of alpha bar, here zero point six four. The noise part has the rest: zero point three six.
variance/sum: The noise is independent of the image, so the variances add: alpha bar, plus one minus alpha bar, is one. That is what the roots are for.
variance/share: So alpha bar is the share of the variance still image: here, sixty four percent image, and thirty six percent noise.
variance/without: Leave the roots out, and a half and half mix has a variance of a quarter plus a quarter: only a half. The middle of the path would fade toward gray.
variance/spread: That holds only when the image starts at a variance of one. Start it at two, and the image part is zero point six four times two: one point two eight.
variance/total: The noise part still adds zero point three six, so x t has a variance of one point six four.
schedule/steps: A diffusion model splits the path into many steps, say a thousand, and gives every step t its own alpha bar.
schedule/falls: At step zero, alpha bar is one: the clean image. It falls as t grows, and by the last step it is close to zero: almost pure noise.
schedule/sched: That list of values is the noise schedule: it sets how fast the image fades.
schedule/ho: In 2020, Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel used a schedule that fades fast: by step five hundred, under a tenth of the variance is image.
schedule/cosine: In 2021, Alex Nichol and Prafulla Dhariwal found it destroys the image faster than it needs to: the last quarter of the steps is almost pure noise. Their cosine schedule, like this one, keeps about half at step five hundred.
schedule/jump: And since each blend is one formula from x zero, any step can be made directly, without the steps before it.
